A rename the host writes no frame for is published by the pull's own diff (packages/bridge-core/src/session-diff.ts compares consecutive get_state reads): a changed title publishes session.renamed, a member of EventManifest.ServerDefinitions and of the client store's own switch, an unchanged pull publishes nothing, and the live case observes it on the shipping stream without a duplicate. Measured limits on host 5.1.75 / engine 2026.11.15-2: no archive command is declared or accepted (archive_session, unarchive_session and set_session_archived refuse as Unknown command, get_protocol_info declares no archive method, and none of the 42 get_state keys nor the list_sessions rows carries an archive/trash/hidden/pinned field), so session.archived/unarchived are not emitted rather than invented; move_session is a session-file relocation protocol (moveId plus op prepare|cancel|status|export|import|finish|revoke|copy|identity) that leaves get_state.cwd unchanged, and reopening a session at another cwd produces a different session, so session.moved keeps its only producer, the pull diff on get_state.cwd, pinned by unit test; session.updated is not a carrier (the server manifest has no such type, only a legacy V1 one).

An `error` stop emits neither execution event because the retry records (`auto_retry_end`) already carry `.failed`. These events do not move the TUI's busy/idle registry: that state comes from the host's `session_status` frames through `applyLiveStatus` (`packages/cli/src/bridge-run.ts:625-630`, applied on every status frame at `:1372`), so a finished turn stops reading as busy there. The execution outcomes feed the notification and usage consumers instead (`packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/system/notifications.ts:72-78`, `packages/tui/src/component/usage.tsx:220`); the TUI's own running indicator is not asserted by an end-to-end case, only the events and those subscriptions.

The block boundary (session.text.ended / session.reasoning.ended) keeps travelling beside it for a consumer on the older member. items.semanticDifference: delivered as a bridge-side rule surface that the client sees as its own contract: the host keeps no per-session rule document and emits no session.permissions frame, its gate being one approval preset per session plus a select dialog per gated call, so the bridge keeps the document itself (packages/bridge-core/src/permission-rules.ts, the client's own Permission.Rule shape, read from <config>/bridge-permissions.json, absent = no rules), publishes a session.permissions event in the client's own vocabulary whenever the effective set changes (id evt_*, durable {aggregateID, seq, version: 1}; measured: initial load, edit and clear publish, a re-report publishes nothing), exposes the same set on SessionInfo.permissions, and enforces it in the TUI data layer before a dialog is surfaced: allow answers the host's Allow once, deny answers Deny with feedback and fills the host's follow-up Feedback input dialog with the rule's reason so the model reads it, ask and no match surface the dialog as before; session.permission.reply is implemented (once/always/reject) and the command palette's /rules entry opens a read-only list of each session's rules with effect, action, resource and deny reason. Measured limits: the rules are bridge state, so the host's own preset stays the outer boundary - under a preset that raises no dialog the host never consults a rule and a deny rule has nothing to refuse - and the list is read-only (editing is the trimmed permission.saved row, P-667).

items.targetCapability: client MCP path plus companion extension
items.semanticDifference: measured end to end through the product's own startup path: the launcher composes connectBridgeMcp at startup with the tui server's open_terminal/write_terminal served from the in-process PTY service, the reply frame carries this connection's routing handle, a tui.pack.mcp.request published into BridgeData runs through the shipped executor and is answered by the extension's own handler, and launchBridgeTui now stages the companion extension's host profile before it dials: packages/cli/src/bridge-agent-profile.ts merges {extensions:[<entry>]} into <agentDir>/settings.json, resolved from --key-record, preserving every other key, refusing an unreadable, non-object or symlinked document, writing 0600 through an O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW temporary file and rename, and staging nothing when no entry is present or configured. Measured: the launcher's own function wrote the profile (action updated, the seeded defaultModel survived), the official 5.1.75 image started from those bytes loaded the extension, bridge.mcp.register answered registered:['live-stdio'] with no refusal, and the host->TUI->executor->reply->result round trip completed; removing the launcher's call or the module's write makes the unit suite fail (11 pass becomes 10/1 and 8/3). Limits: a host already running before the launcher's first run picks the entry up on its next start (settings.json is read at host start), the launcher dials a host rather than starting one in this tree, and a built dist-bridge ships no extension, so a binary stages only when the entry sits beside it or BRIDGE_COMPANION_EXTENSION names it.
